brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases: piece:0,0,0 full, piece:1,0,0 full, piece:0,1,0 full, and piece:0,-1,0 half-n, grouped in a small cluster on level 0. Open faces capped and joints bolted (lockJoints); check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut (classic style, key s) added on the cut face of the half-n base at (0,-1).

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike at junction (0,0),(0,1),(1,0), where the three full bases meet at level 0.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm applied to that mount spike (a solid spike refused the platform; mount variant accepted it).

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: three full hex bases in a triangle plus a half base, with a drawer on the half base's cut face. A mount spike sits at the corner where the three full bases meet and carries a small platform. Caps and joint bolts were applied as house rules; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. No props were added since the brief did not call for any. Material suitability and load strength are not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
